_meta.description: World lithium mine production and reserves, USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 (February 2026), Lithium chapter by Brian W. Jaskula.
_meta.source: U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Lithium
_meta.units: metric tons of LITHIUM CONTENT (Li), not lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE).

lce_conversion.derivation: Li2CO3 molar mass 73.89 g/mol divided by 2 x 6.94 g/mol for Li. Standard stoichiometry, computed by us, not a USGS figure.

_meta.extraction_note: The USGS PDF table lost its footnote spacing when text was extracted, so 'Argentina 2024 = 513,800' and 'Chile 2024 = 548,900' were read as 13,800 and 48,900 (a footnote digit '5' = 'Reported' got glued on). Same issue for Australia reserves: '68,400,000' is 8,400,000 with footnote '6' attached. Check: reserves of all rows sum to 36.47 Mt against USGS's 37 Mt total (they would sum to 96 Mt with the glued digit). Production check: the nine producing countries' 2024 values sum to 222,970 against USGS's rounded world total of 222,000 (which excludes the US); with the glued digits the sum would be over 1,000,000. The 2025 column sums to 288,380 against 290,000. Please eyeball these two cells against the PDF before presenting.
_meta.us_production_note: US production is withheld by USGS (W) and excluded from the world totals.

ev_lithium_per_vehicle_t_lce.note: From the project brief (about 8 kg LCE per EV). ASSUMPTION, configurable in the calc engine. Not from USGS. Real values depend on battery size and chemistry.

world.mine_production_note: Excludes US production. 2025 is a USGS estimate ('e').

price_usd_per_t_lithium_carbonate.note: US annual average, real dollars, battery grade

countries.name: Australia
countries.reserves_note: USGS footnote: JORC-compliant reserves were 5.1 million tons
